source: The figures the model can compute, each with what it needs. Formulas are functions in moneymodels/engines/model.js keyed by id; this file names the inputs, the tier, the unit and what the figure is for. Tier N may need only facts from bands 1 to N (linted in moneymodels/test/run.js).
confidenceNote: The thresholds on ratio30 (1 and 2) and ltgpCac (3) are the book's rules of thumb.
note: kind: 'number' (a figure), 'badge' (earned by finishing levels), 'chart' (a picture), 'read' (a sentence). unit: cents, percent, ratio, count, days, months, text. A recipe with no formula in the engine is a lint failure.

recipes.label: You know what a money model is
recipes.says: The sequence, the cash constraint, the four offers.

recipes.label: You know the attraction plays
recipes.says: The door, six ways to build it, the three parts it needs.

recipes.label: You know the upsell plays
recipes.says: The moment after yes, four plays, and the ask.

recipes.label: You know the downsell plays
recipes.says: The smaller yes, four plays, where it sits.

recipes.label: You know the continuity plays
recipes.says: One sale into many, five plays, churn.

recipes.label: You know the six numbers
recipes.says: The numbers, the two thresholds, the four ways to grow.

recipes.label: Gross profit per sale, today
recipes.says: What one sale of your main offer leaves after delivering it.

recipes.label: Gross margin, today
recipes.says: The share of the price you keep after delivery. Above 50% is where most of the plays become affordable.

recipes.label: Cost of a customer (CAC)
recipes.says: What you spent to get customers, divided by the customers you got.

recipes.label: First sale minus the cost of the customer
recipes.says: Gross profit on the first sale, less what the customer cost. Negative means the first sale does not pay for the customer, which is exactly what the rest of the model is for.

recipes.label: Customers you can afford per month
recipes.says: Cash for getting customers divided by the cost of one. The scale ceiling before the model self-funds.

recipes.label: Cost per lead
recipes.says: Spend divided by leads.

recipes.label: Customers the funnel implies
recipes.says: Leads times the attraction conversion rate. Compare with the customers you counted.

recipes.label: Attraction offer gross profit
recipes.says: Price less delivery, per buyer.

recipes.label: Upsell gross profit
recipes.says: Per taker.

recipes.label: Upsell profit per customer
recipes.says: Upsell gross profit times the take rate: what the upsell adds to every customer on average.

recipes.label: Downsell gross profit
recipes.says: Per taker.

recipes.label: Downsell profit per customer
recipes.says: Downsell gross profit, times the share who said no to the upsell, times the downsell take rate.

recipes.label: Continuity gross profit per month
recipes.says: Per member, per month.

recipes.label: Months a member stays, on average
recipes.says: One divided by monthly churn.

recipes.label: Continuity lifetime profit per customer
recipes.says: Monthly gross profit, times the months a member stays, times the share who join.

recipes.label: 30-day cash collected per customer (planned)
recipes.says: Cash before delivery costs: the figure to compare with what you counted at the bank. The gross profit twin is the headline.

recipes.label: 30-day cash per customer (planned)
recipes.says: Gross profit the sequence collects from one customer in their first 30 days, assuming every offer is made inside the month. Prove levels U10, D10 and C10 check that.

recipes.label: 30-day ratio (planned)
recipes.says: 30-day cash divided by the cost of a customer. 1 is break even, 2 is self-funding.

recipes.label: The most you could pay for a customer
recipes.says: Half the 30-day cash: the cost of a customer that still leaves you self-funding.

recipes.label: Lifetime gross profit per customer (LTGP)
recipes.says: Everything the sequence earns from one customer, less delivery, over their whole stay.

recipes.label: LTGP to CAC
recipes.says: How many times over a customer pays for themselves. The book wants at least 3.

recipes.label: 30-day cash per lead
recipes.says: What a lead is worth to you in the first month, so you know what you can pay for one.

recipes.label: Room to grow before capacity
recipes.says: Customers per month you could add before you cannot serve them.

recipes.label: Customers a month to cover fixed costs
recipes.says: Fixed costs divided by 30-day cash per customer. Above this, the month is profitable on new customers alone.

recipes.label: Where a customer's first-month cash goes
recipes.says: Delivery, the cost of the customer, and what is left.

recipes.label: The 30-day cash, offer by offer
recipes.says: Each offer's gross profit stacked against the cost of the customer, with the two threshold lines.

recipes.label: The sequence as a funnel
recipes.says: From 100 leads: who buys, who goes bigger, who takes the smaller yes, who keeps paying.

recipes.label: Members left, month by month
recipes.says: A cohort of 100 joiners at your churn rate, for a year.

recipes.label: Customers per month if you reinvest
recipes.says: Twelve months, buying customers with last month's 30-day cash, capped at capacity.

recipes.label: The model's health, six ways
recipes.says: Margin, 30-day ratio, LTGP to CAC, upsell take, retention and conversion, each against a target.

recipes.label: The promise
